title: Adaptive region prioritization and graceful request degradation
creator: Priya Rao
description: Design and implement an adaptive regional prioritization system that combines latency-based routing, probabilistic geo-prioritization (soft-pinning), and capacity-aware admission control to preserve SLOs during regional degradation. Deliverables: routing decision service (decider) that emits decisions and metrics, circuit-breaker integration with per-region token-buckets, and an admission/load-shedding policy that respects tenant latency budgets and global cost budgets. The solution must support gradual rollout, observability (per-route SLO heatmaps, shed metrics), and operator runbooks for forced failover and emergency shedding.
acceptance_criteria: Routing decider service responds < 5ms p50 for 99% of eval traffic in lab and is horizontally scalable
Traffic shifts to secondary regions under configured latency/capacity thresholds with < 2x error amplification
Circuit-breaker trips per-region and per-model when regional CPU/GPU utilization or queue latency exceeds thresholds, and produces clear metrics in console
Load-shedding policy enforces per-tenant SLAs: high-tier tenants see graceful degradation (reduced token limit / condensed batching) while low-tier receives adaptive rejects; documented in runbook
End-to-end test harness reproduces a region outage and validates failover + shed behavior within 30s and meets SLOs for priority customers
Monitoring dashboards (SLO, shed rate, rejected requests, region-utilization) are live and have alert rules with runbook links
tasks: Write design doc: trade-offs for probabilistic pinning vs deterministic geo-pin and hedging strategies
Prototype routing-decider API + simulator for latency/capacity signals
Implement per-region circuit-breaker library and integrate with request router
Implement admission controller with tenant priority tiers and token-bucket shaping
Create canary rollout plan and feature flagging in console
Add metrics, dashboards, and alerting; wire runbooks and incident playbooks
End-to-end chaos test: simulate region latency spike, resource exhaustion, and full region outage
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope: prioritize latency-first routing, then capacity hints; will use probabilistic soft-pinning to reduce cold start of secondary regions.
2025-02-18: Proto decider simulator implemented (Marcus). Initial results: probabilistic pinning reduces tail latency amplification in secondary regions vs immediate full failover.
2025-02-25: Design review with PM and SRE. Feedback: add tenant-aware shedding rules and explicit quota fallback for dedicated customers. Security requested KMS usage for routing config secrets.
2025-03-01: PR #7891 opened for decider API and circuit-breaker library. Integration tests failing intermittently under high concurrency; suspected race in token-bucket refill path.
2025-03-04: Fixed race in token-bucket (see PR #7906). Running full e2e chaos tests in staging (expected results tomorrow).
decisions: Use conservative default: latency-based primary choice, then probabilistic soft-pin to secondary regions with annealing over time (start 90% primary, decay to 50% over 60s under degraded conditions)
Circuit-breaker thresholds: trigger when request queue latency > 300ms p95 or GPU utilization > 92% sustained for 30s
Load-shedding strategy: class-based admission controller (gold/silver/bronze). Gold gets prioritized batching and KV-cache-prefetch; bronze receives 429 with Retry-After when shedding needed
Hedging: limited hedges (single additional parallel request) only for gold tenants and only when p95 latency exceeds SLO by 20%
Observability: emit routing_decision, decision_reason, origin_region, target_region, shed_reason, circuit_state as tags for all requests
